class_feedback.comment_comparing_conditions: I liked the task and it was pretty fun to do; one thing I would suggest is making it a bit more complex so that it is not as identifiable, as I feel the AI would serve more of a purpose when the statements are a bit more complex.

I think the AI is not that accurate because some articles that I was confident are not satire was being classified as satire. After I found out that the AI is not that helpful, I found myself not trusting it's outputs much and using my own instincts instead for both cases. AI did help increase my confidence in predictions though

I like the quirkyness of the usecase, having AI determine which words played a role in AI's decision was good to include, However when asking the user's about how sure they were now, after AI's answer could be framed in a better way, it is confusing on what is being asked here to rate AI's response or to rate my answer after seeing AI's. I also noticed a lot of times the AI's response was not reliable
class_feedback.other_notes: For the run with AI the Instructions had too much text, divide it into bullet points shorter and increase the font a bit...

class_feedback.comment_comparing_conditions: It is difficult to tell a difference sometimes. Because AI only looks at the word, so I don't trust it a lot. AI and I often have a different answers, so I think I will have a lower confidence in my choices with AI.

The first time, without AI, I got 20/20, but with AI assistance I got 18/20. This may have just been luck, but it does seem like this model wasn't particularly good. For the most part the satire seemed obvious, so it could be that the model can lead people to overthink and over-rely? The specific attention the model paid to each word was interesting, at times it felt like I was able to write-off a conflicting ai output based on a disribution that didn't make sense.

The AI proved pretty unhelpful. I was shown why the AI made the decisions it did but the underlining of words classified as satire vs genuine didn't give me as an analyst any information to work off of. It would have been nice to recieve a reasoning excerpt alongside the confidence score to get a better idea of why a title is being classified the way it is. It also seemed like the AI was often wrong as it would mark what I thought was obviously satire or obviously real as the exact opposite underlining words that made me think it was one option as evidence that it was the other. It seems to be weighing political text as satire regardless of the overall context of the title.
class_feedback.other_notes: I liked the way the confidence score was shown. It was very visually appealing.

comments.comment: it was a fun exercise. I would really like a back button which gives the user 10 seconds to update their answer.
would have loved the questions that i got right or wrong for both sections. Also, hope to see how AI impacted/compared against my scores/options.
I could be wrong on a lot of these

I would say the length of the task could be reduced as I think these were a bit easier to identify; I would suggest making the sentences a bit more complex or targeting a particular set of domains or scenarios.
I found myself being more confident selecting what was satire than selecting what might have been real.

The AI suggestion often seemed wrong or uninformative. I also am realizing now when I was told to revaluate my answer I may have been able to change my selection or "real" or "satire" instead of just the confidence rating, but I'm not sure if that was an option.
